look_here_first: Inspect the spurred yellow flower from the side, then compare mature capsules and seeds with C. micrantha. Golden corydalis typically has 13–16 mm flowers, and its fruits may spread or hang and curve; seed margin and fruit position depend on subspecies, so neither alone is decisive.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Small, often spreading to ascending, delicate annual or biennial herb with multiple slender stems.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Alternate, petiolate, finely divided two to three times into rounded or oval ultimate segments; often bluish green.

key_traits.label: Flowers
key_traits.text: Bilateral, yellow, four petals, one outer petal with a rearward spur; racemes of several to many flowers; corolla often about 13–16 mm including 4–5 mm spur.

key_traits.label: Fruits
key_traits.text: Slender capsules about 15–25 mm, spreading to pendent or sometimes erect depending on subspecies; mature seed and capsule characters important.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Side view of flower showing spur and crest

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Mature capsule angle and shape, interpreted with subspecies variation

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Seed size and marginal ring under magnification

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Flower raceme relative to nearby leaves, not alone
